Each day shows the share of checks that passed. A day drawn pale is one where fewer checks ran than the every-10-minute schedule expects - the scheduler itself missed passes - so there is less evidence about that day; hover it for how many ran. We show it rather than hiding it, but a day whose every check passed is not counted against the service because we looked less often. The price floor is not the price endpoints. It is a cached copy of every price, rewritten once a minute, that a cold Cloudflare location serves instantly instead of waiting on the exchanges; a failed check means that rewrite stopped happening, so those requests paid the live round trip - slower, not unavailable. GET /api/v1/price answers either way, and its own latency is on the API page. Thin venues (dYdX, Bitfinex) legitimately go hours without a liquidation; a connected socket with an old last event is quiet, not broken. Machine-readable: GET /api/status, external monitors can use GET /api/health (200 while the scheduler is alive). Changes to the API: RSS.
